scope: AIOC-only preimplementation contract closure; no Multiversal-app runtime implementation

authority.device_context_and_remote_continuity: SMB-02; device identity is connection/recovery context only and is never subject, membership or role authority
authority.policy_boundary: Client or device possession authenticates only the bound subject/session; Campaign membership, role, Character control, entitlement and authoritative mutation remain separate decisions.

local_proof_of_possession.baseline_credential: per-device asymmetric signing credential bound to one canonical subject through A3/identity-device
local_proof_of_possession.baseline_algorithm_profile: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256; any future substitution requires explicit contract revision and equivalent-or-stronger approved security
local_proof_of_possession.private_key_rule: Generate on-device and keep in operating-system secure key storage. Routine device private keys are non-exportable by default and never appear in ordinary product documents, logs, diagnostics, sync records or wire messages.
local_proof_of_possession.establishment_rule: Production StableSubjectSession establishment MUST consume a verified authentication-proof receipt. Direct subjectId+identityId assertion remains test/local-alpha-only behavior and is forbidden for production-local or remote caller authentication.
local_proof_of_possession.zero_service_rule: The local-first path does not require a hosted identity provider. SMB-01 external/provider IdentityPort remains optional and replaceable rather than a prerequisite for local proof.

invariants: deviceId is a stable installation/device-context identifier and is never a canonical subject identifier
device possession never grants Campaign membership, role, Character control, entitlement or owner authority
one active device binding belongs to exactly one canonical subject
session resume or remote reconnect must prove an active credential whose deviceId matches an active binding
replacement/reinstall creates a new deviceId and device credential; it never silently reuses a revoked device identity

establishment_preconditions: authentication proof is current and replay-safe
credential and device binding belong to the same subject
invalidation_rules: credential revocation invalidates sessions established from that credential
device revocation invalidates sessions for that device
permission or entitlement version drift forces revalidation before protected entry or mutation
session expiry, revocation and sign-out remain fail-closed

peer_identity_binding.rule: After authentication, transport peers are bound to this receipt. Commands, presence and reconnect derive actor/subject/device from the binding. Caller-supplied actorId, subjectId, identityId or deviceId must either be absent or exactly match the binding; mismatch rejects before authorization or mutation.

continuity_identity.rule: Client continuity may not be keyed by subjectId alone. Campaign/Session identity is mandatory; per-device cursors are separated by deviceId without making device identity authoritative.

successful_paths.rule: A current authenticated session on an active device authorizes enrollment of a replacement device credential for the same subject. The replacement receives a new deviceId; the old device may be explicitly revoked.

A user-created explicitly encrypted recovery archive may carry subject-preserving recovery material. Import proves recovery authority, preserves subjectId/identityId, creates a new deviceId/device credential and never silently restores a revoked device binding.

When an approved external identity binding exists, provider-verified recovery may rebind a local credential while ProviderIndependentIdentityMapping preserves the existing canonical subject. This path is optional and is not required for zero-service operation.

recovery_and_rebind.failure_rule: If no governed recovery proof exists, recovery fails closed. The product must not mint a replacement canonical subject and label it recovered, merge subjects automatically, or require administrator/database intervention for the representative BRP-02 success path.
recovery_and_rebind.campaign_rule: Recovery preserves identity only. Existing Campaign membership/ownership remains separately authoritative. A replacement device must be rebound; a new Campaign invitation is required only when membership/invitation authority independently requires it, not merely because the device changed.
recovery_and_rebind.data_rights_rule: Export/deletion requests are subject-scoped, never device-scoped, and cannot cross context boundaries.

product_profile_reconciliation.current_state: PCV-01 ProductProfile directly persists subjectId and identityId strings and therefore represents identifiers, not authentication proof.
required_pcv03a_migration: Treat existing ProductProfile subjectId/identityId as migration inputs only; verify or create canonical IdentityServicePort + ProviderIndependentIdentityMapping records before use as authenticated identity.
Enroll a local proof-of-possession credential and device binding before production StableSubjectSession establishment.

Instantiate production-local adapters for IdentityServicePort, ProviderIndependentIdentityMapping, StableSubjectSessionPort, local proof verification and device binding; do not create PCV-specific parallel identity ownership.
New product profiles must create identity/mapping through canonical owner contracts rather than minting unauthenticated subject/identity strings as sufficient authority.

external_sanity_checks.use: random verifier-generated challenges with sufficient entropy and replay rejection
cryptographic proof of possession, public-key verifier records and replay-resistant challenges
device key material can remain non-exportable and hardware-backed when available

runtime_boundary.next_runtime_destination: PCV-03A after PCV-I01B through PCV-I06 predecessor closure

completion_evidence.note: Contract-level closure only. Runtime implementation remains reserved for PCV-03A after the remaining PCV-PRE predecessors close.
